verses.text: Adoni-Zedek, king of Jerusalem, heard that Joshua had captured Ai and completely destroyed it, doing to Ai and its king what he had done to Jericho and its king. He also heard that the people of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and were living among them.
He and his people were very afraid, because Gibeon was a large city, like one of the royal cities. It was bigger than Ai, and all its men were strong fighters.
So Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem sent a message to Hoham king of Hebron, Piram king of Jarmuth, Japhia king of Lachish and Debir king of Eglon.
He said, "Come and help me attack Gibeon, because it has made peace with Joshua and the people of Israel."
So the five Amorite kings, the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish and Eglon, joined forces. They marched out with all their armies, camped around Gibeon and attacked it.

The men of Gibeon sent a message to Joshua in the camp at Gilgal: "Do not abandon your servants! Come quickly and save us! Help us, because all the Amorite kings from the hill country have joined together against us."
So Joshua marched up from Gilgal with his whole army, including all his best fighting men.
The LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid of them. I have given them into your hands. Not one of them will be able to stand against you."
Joshua marched all night from Gilgal and took them by surprise.
The LORD threw them into panic in front of Israel. Israel defeated them badly at Gibeon and chased them along the road up to Beth Horon, striking them down all the way to Azekah and Makkedah.

As they ran from Israel down the road from Beth Horon, the LORD threw huge hailstones down on them from the sky all the way to Azekah, and they died. More of them died from the hail than from the swords of the Israelites.
On the day the LORD gave the Amorites to Israel, Joshua spoke to the LORD. In front of all Israel he said, "Sun, stand still over Gibeon! Moon, stop over the Valley of Aijalon!"

So the sun stood still and the moon stopped until the nation had beaten its enemies. This is written in the Book of Jashar. The sun stopped in the middle of the sky and waited about a whole day before going down.
There has never been a day like it, before or since, when the LORD listened to a human voice like that. Surely the LORD was fighting for Israel!
Then Joshua and all Israel went back to the camp at Gilgal.
Now the five kings had run away and hidden in a cave at Makkedah.
Someone told Joshua, "The five kings have been found hiding in the cave at Makkedah."
Joshua said, "Roll large stones over the mouth of the cave, and put men there to guard it.
But do not stop! Chase your enemies and attack them from behind. Do not let them reach their cities, because the LORD your God has given them into your hands."
Joshua and the Israelites defeated them very badly, almost wiping them out. The few who survived escaped into their walled cities.
Then all the army came back safely to Joshua in the camp at Makkedah. After that, no one dared to say a word against the Israelites.
Joshua said, "Open the mouth of the cave and bring those five kings out to me."
So they brought the five kings out of the cave: the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish and Eglon.

When they brought the kings to Joshua, he called all the men of Israel. He said to the army commanders who had come with him, "Come here and put your feet on the necks of these kings." So they came and put their feet on their necks.
Joshua said to them, "Do not be afraid or lose heart. Be strong and brave. This is what the LORD will do to all the enemies you fight."
Then Joshua struck and killed the kings and hung them on five trees. They hung there until evening.
At sunset Joshua ordered them to be taken down from the trees and thrown into the cave where they had hidden. Large stones were placed over the mouth of the cave, and they are still there today.

That day Joshua captured Makkedah. He killed its king and everyone in the city with the sword. He completely destroyed it and left no survivors. He did to the king of Makkedah what he had done to the king of Jericho.
Then Joshua and all Israel moved on from Makkedah to Libnah and attacked it.
The LORD gave Libnah and its king into Israel's hands too. Joshua killed everyone in the city with the sword and left no survivors. He did to its king what he had done to the king of Jericho.
Then Joshua and all Israel moved on from Libnah to Lachish. They camped around it and attacked it.
The LORD gave Lachish into Israel's hands, and Joshua captured it on the second day. He killed everyone in it with the sword, just as he had done to Libnah.
Then Horam king of Gezer came to help Lachish, but Joshua defeated him and his army, leaving no survivors.
Then Joshua and all Israel moved on from Lachish to Eglon. They camped around it and attacked it.
They captured it that same day and killed everyone in it with the sword. Joshua completely destroyed it, as he had done to Lachish.
Then Joshua and all Israel went up from Eglon to Hebron and attacked it.
They captured it and killed its king, everyone in it, and the people of its villages with the sword. They left no survivors. Just as at Eglon, they completely destroyed it and everyone in it.
Then Joshua and all Israel turned and attacked Debir.

They captured the city, its king and its villages, and killed everyone in it with the sword. They left no survivors. Joshua did to Debir and its king what he had done to Hebron and to Libnah and its king.

So Joshua conquered the whole region: the hill country, the Negev in the south, the western foothills and the mountain slopes, with all their kings. He left no survivors. He completely destroyed everything that breathed, just as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded.
Joshua conquered them from Kadesh Barnea to Gaza, and the whole region of Goshen as far as Gibeon.
Joshua captured all these kings and their lands in one campaign, because the LORD, the God of Israel, fought for Israel.
Then Joshua and all Israel went back to the camp at Gilgal.
